claim.pdf_says: D.9.2.3   Examples   (fourth-level subclause, same rank as D.9.2.1 General and D.9.2.2 Restricted data-pointers on p1095)
claim.markdown_says: ## D.9.2.3 Examples   (level 2, while its siblings are '#### D.9.2.1 General' and '#### D.9.2.2 Restricted data-pointers' and its parent is '### D.9.2 Data-addresses and data-pointers')
claim.why_it_matters: D.9.2.3 is promoted two levels, out from under D.9.2 and up to the rank of D.9 itself, so the outline detaches the Examples subclause from the data-pointer discussion it belongs to. Same page-boundary signature as the D.8.2/D.8.3 case: D.9.2.3 is the first heading on page 1096.

verdict.reasoning:
I tried to refute this on every available ground and could not.

PRINTED GLYPHS, page 1096 (spec_p1096.png @300dpi): the only heading on the page reads 'D.9.2.3   Examples', bold, flush with the body-text left margin, with the wide en-space between number and title that ISO uses for every numbered subclause. I rendered page 1095 for a direct rank comparison. It prints 'D.9   Addresses and pointers', 'D.9.1   General', 'D.9.2   Data-addresses and data-pointers', 'D.9.2.1   General', 'D.9.2.2   Restricted data-pointers' — all in the same bold face at the same left margin, distinguished ONLY by the depth of the dotted number. 'D.9.2.3   Examples' on p1096 is typographically indistinguishable from 'D.9.2.1   General' and 'D.9.2.2   Restricted data-pointers' on p1095. In any case the dotted number D.9.2.3 is by itself dispositive: it is a fourth-level subclause and a child of D.9.2.

MARKDOWN, specs/ISO_COBOL.md (line numbers verified by grep '^#+ D\.9'):
  43932  ## D.9 Addresses and pointers
  43935  ### D.9.1 General
  43948  ### D.9.2 Data-addresses and data-pointers
  43951  #### D.9.2.1 General
  43960  #### D.9.2.2 Restricted data-pointers
  43979  ## D.9.2.3 Examples          <-- level 2
  44050  ## D.9.3 Program-addresses, function-addresses, program-pointers and function-pointers
The claim quotes both sources exactly. D.9.2.3 is emitted at '##', i.e. a peer of '## D.9', two levels above where its siblings sit.

REFUTATION ATTEMPTS, all failed:
  - 'The text is present, just reflowed' — no. The heading text IS present and correct; the defect is not missing text but a wrong nesting level, which is exactly what the claim asserts. The 'missing-heading' kind label is the ledger's bucket name, not a claim that the string is absent.
  - 'Page-break furniture' — no. A page marker ('## Page 1096') and a running header ('# ISO/IEC 1989:2023 (E)') are furniture and are correctly present at lines 43971/43974; the D.9.2.3 heading at 43979 is body structure, and its level is wrong independently of the furniture.
  - 'Wrapping / hyphenation / formatting only' — no. Markdown heading depth is the sole encoding of outline parentage in this transcription; changing it changes the document tree that every TOC, outline extractor and anchor-walk consumes.
  - 'Does not change meaning' — partially mitigating but not exculpating; see below.

The page-boundary signature the claim names is confirmed and is a real recurring pattern, not a coincidence: D.9.2.3 is the first heading on page 1096; the identically-shaped D.8 case is present in the same file (43777 '## D.8 Types', 43780 '### D.8.1 General', then 43811 '## D.8.2 Weakly-typed items' and 43840 '## D.8.3 Strongly-typed group items', both flattened to level 2).
verdict.corrected_description:
CONFIRMED, with two corrections/extensions to the original write-up.

(1) Scope is wider than one heading. The flattening is not self-limiting at D.9.2.3 — the outline never re-nests afterward. Downstream of the break the whole D.9.3 subtree is promoted one level as well: line 44050 '## D.9.3 ...' (should be '###', to match its true siblings '### D.9.1' and '### D.9.2'), 44053 '### D.9.3.1 General' and 44062 '### D.9.3.2 Restricted program-pointers and function-pointers' (both should be '####', to match '#### D.9.2.1' / '#### D.9.2.2'). So the correct repair is not a single-line edit: D.9.2.3 must go '##' -> '####', and then D.9.3 '##' -> '###' with D.9.3.1 and D.9.3.2 '###' -> '####'. Note D.9.3 and its children are on page 1097, so a page-1096-only fix leaves the subtree still misnested.

(2) Severity is navigational, not semantic. No prose is lost, altered or reordered — page 1096's body text (the strongly-typed-group-item paragraph, the Get-next-record prototype, the REPOSITORY/my-wreck example, the CALL ... RETURNING p and SET ADDRESS OF sequence, and the p2/data-record API example) transcribes faithfully against the render, and critically the subclause NUMBER 'D.9.2.3' survives verbatim inside the heading text. A human or tool citing '§D.9.2.3' therefore still resolves correctly, and no citation is destroyed. What breaks is the derived structure: any TOC build, outline walk, parent-scoped search, or 'give me all of D.9.2' extraction will drop the Examples subclause out of D.9.2 and hoist it to the rank of D.9, and will likewise mis-parent all of D.9.3. Structural severity is the right classification; it should not be escalated to content-loss.

(3) The pattern is mechanical and worth sweeping globally rather than fixing case by case: every instance found so far (D.8.2, D.8.3, D.9.2.3, D.9.3) is a heading that falls first on a fresh PDF page, which the transcription pipeline appears to emit at a fixed '##' depth instead of the depth implied by its dotted number. A repo-wide pass that re-derives heading level from the dot-count of the clause number would fix the whole class in one change; the ledger should carry this as one systemic defect with per-page instances, not as N independent findings.
